commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Guru-Tattva and Shiva-Abheda
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes that the Guru is not a separate entity from the ultimate reality (Shiva). By identifying the Guru with the cosmic principles of Nada, Bindu, and Kala, it posits that the teacher is the manifest path to the unmanifest absolute.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This emphasizes the significance of the Guru-Shishya parampara, framing the teacher as a psychological and spiritual conduit who facilitates the student's inner awakening.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice prescribed is Mangalacharana, invoking the Guru's grace as a prerequisite for embarking on the higher practices of Rajayoga (Samadhi), acknowledging the need to clear obstacles (Vighna) via spiritual surrender.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept explores Shiva-Abheda (non-difference from Shiva) within the Guru-Tattva, where the Guru is realized as the union of Nada (primal frequency), Bindu (cosmic point of concentration), and Kala (the manifest energy of consciousness).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the vital importance of mentorship and the surrender of the ego to a higher principle or teacher. In a modern context, it suggests that success in complex tasks (like deep meditative practices) requires an auspicious mental orientation and a recognition of the 'inner guide' to navigate potential mental or situational barriers.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
समाधिक्रमं प्रतिजानीते -
आत्यन्तिकस्वरूपावस्थानं प्रतिप्रसवसिद्धम् । व्युत्थाननिरोधसमाधिसंस्कारा मनसि लीयन्ते । मनोऽस्मितायाम् अस्मिता महति महान् प्रधान इति चित्तगुणानां प्रतिप्रसवः स्वकरणे लयः । ननु जीवन्मुक्तस्य व्युत्थाने ब्राह्मणोऽहं मनुष्योऽहम् इत्यादिव्यवहारदर्शनात् चित्तादिभिः औपाधिकभावजननात् अम्लेन दुग्धयेव स्वरूपच्युतिः स्यादिति चेन्न । संप्रज्ञातसमाधौ अनुभूतात्मसंस्कारस्य निरोधसंस्कारस्य च तदानीं सत्वात् । ताभ्यां च व्युत्थानसंस्कारस्य दग्धबीजकल्पत्वात् व्युत्थानव्यवहारस्य अतात्विकत्वनिश्चयात् । अतात्विकान्यथाभावस्य विकारित्वाप्रयोजकत्वात् । अम्लेन दुग्धस्य दधिभावस्तु तात्विक इति दृष्टान्तवैषम्यात् । पुरुषस्य तु अन्तःकरणोपाधिकोऽहं ब्राह्मण इत्यादिव्यवहारः स्फटिकस्य जपाकुसुमसंनिधानोपाधिररुणिमेव न तात्त्विकः । जपाकुसुपागमे स्फटिकस्य स्वरूपस्थितिवत् अन्तःकरणस्य सकलवृत्तिनिरोधे स्वस्वरूपावस्थितिः अच्युतैव पुरुषस्य ॥ २ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text introduces the sequence of Samadhi as follows: The ultimate resting in one's own nature is established through 'Pratiprasava' (involution). The impressions (Samskaras) of Vyuṭṭhana (external engagement), Nirodha (restraint), and Samadhi merge into the mind. The mind dissolves into Asmita (egoity), Asmita into Mahat (intellect), and Mahat into Pradhana (Nature); this is the 'Pratiprasava' of the Gunas of the Chitta, their dissolution into their cause. If one asks, 'Since the Jivanmukta is seen in external life behaving as a Brahmin or human, does this association with adjuncts (Upadhi) not cause a loss of true nature, like milk curdling when exposed to acid?' The answer is 'No.' Because the impressions of the Samprajnata Samadhi and the impressions of Nirodha are present at that time. Through these, the external impressions become like burnt seeds; thus, external behavior is known as non-essential. A non-essential change does not imply a change in the essence. The example of curdled milk is faulty because the transformation of milk into curd is real/essential. The behavior of the Purusha identifying as a 'Brahmin' due to the adjunct of the Antahkarana is like the redness of a crystal appearing due to a Japa flower; it is not essential. When the flower is removed, the crystal returns to its state, just as the Purusha, upon the cessation of all mental fluctuations, rests established in his true nature, unchanging.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: समाधिक्रम को प्रतिपादित करते हैं - स्वरूप में आत्यन्तिक अवस्थान 'प्रतिप्रसव' से सिद्ध होता है। व्युत्थान, निरोध और समाधि के संस्कार मन में लीन हो जाते हैं। मन अस्मिता में, अस्मिता महत्तत्त्व में, और महत्तत्त्व प्रधान में लीन हो जाता है, यही चित्त के गुणों का प्रतिप्रसव अर्थात् कारण में लय है। यदि शंका हो कि जीवन्मुक्त के व्युत्थान काल में 'मैं ब्राह्मण हूँ', 'मैं मनुष्य हूँ' आदि व्यवहार देखने से, चित्तादि उपाधियों के कारण क्या दूध में अम्ल मिलने के समान स्वरूपच्युति नहीं होगी? तो उत्तर है - नहीं। क्योंकि उस समय संप्रज्ञात समाधि के अनुभवजन्य संस्कार और निरोध संस्कार विद्यमान रहते हैं। उनके कारण व्युत्थान संस्कार 'दग्धबीज' कल्प हो जाते हैं, अतः व्युत्थान व्यवहार अतात्त्विक सिद्ध होता है। अतात्त्विक विकार वास्तविक परिवर्तन का प्रयोजक नहीं होता। दूध का दही बनना तात्त्विक परिवर्तन है, अतः दृष्टान्त विषम है। पुरुष का अन्त:करणोपाधिक 'मैं ब्राह्मण हूँ' आदि व्यवहार तो स्फटिक में जपाकुसुम के सामीप्य से प्रतीत होने वाली अरुणिमा के समान है, वास्तविक नहीं। जपाकुसुम के हटने पर स्फटिक का अपने स्वरूप में रहना ही है, जैसे चित्त की वृत्तियों के निरोध होने पर पुरुष अपने स्वरूप में अच्युत रूप से स्थित होता है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi-Krama (The progression of meditative absorption)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse introduces the systematic process through which the mind transcends its worldly modifications to rest in its original state (Svarupa). It emphasizes that Samadhi is not a random state but a structured path of involution where mental qualities dissolve into their causal substrata.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as the foundational methodology for self-realization in Indian psychology, providing a structured approach to focus and awareness in an age characterized by mental fragmentation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practices are Samadhi, Nirodha (restraint of mental modifications), and sustained introspection (Samskara management) to reach the state of Pratyak-cetana.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Pratiprasava (involution of Gunas) and the distinction between Upadhi (adjunct) and Svarupa (Self). It highlights that Jivanmukti is the state where the mind's modifications are rendered inert (burnt seeds), leaving the Purusha in an unperturbed Svarupa-avasthiti.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the psychological distinction between the 'acting self' (identity/social mask) and the 'witnessing self' (conscious awareness). It offers a model for managing stress and identity crisis by understanding the ephemeral nature of transient roles (Upadhis).

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Advaita / Yoga-Samadhi
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse equates various technical yogic terms to demonstrate that they represent the same non-dual state of consciousness where the mind ceases to function as a separate entity. It emphasizes that beneath the diversity of yogic terminology lies the unitary experience of transcendent reality.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This is highly relevant in Hatha and Raja Yoga traditions (like the Hathayogapradipika) to prevent confusion regarding nomenclature. In contemporary discourse, it serves as a reminder that various meditative techniques converge into a single psychological state of stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Meditation (Dhyana), breath control (Pranayama leading to Kevala Kumbhaka), and sustained focus on the internal consciousness.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Cittavritti-nirodha' where 'Rājayoga', 'Samādhi', 'Unmanī', and 'Manonmanī' are synonymous labels for the state of 'Manolaya'—the dissolution of the mental modifications.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this equates to achieving a 'flow state' or mindfulness where the ego-centric narrative of the mind is silent, offering a therapeutic detachment from chronic stress and existential anxiety.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi and Non-duality
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the state of the ultimate consciousness or the nature of Samadhi. It posits that true liberation involves transcending the limitations of the mind, realizing the non-dual essence of reality, and remaining detached from all material supports or impurities.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These terms are central to Advaita Vedanta and Hatha Yoga traditions. In a modern context, they represent the psychological state of 'de-identification' with ego and thoughts, promoting mindfulness and mental clarity.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Dhyana (meditation), Vairagya (detachment), and the cultivation of the witness consciousness (Sakshi-bhava).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on Amanaskata (the state of mindlessness/thoughtlessness), Advaita (Non-duality), Niralambata (unsupported awareness), and Niranjanata (purity of Atman).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this equates to achieving a state of deep flow or 'no-mind,' allowing one to observe stressors without becoming attached to them, thus reducing anxiety.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Advaita / Samadhi
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse illustrates the nature of Samadhi (deep meditative absorption) using the metaphor of salt dissolving in water. It suggests that while the individual essence (the salt) seems distinct, it is ultimately non-different from the substratum (the water) upon full integration.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a core psychological teaching for overcoming the duality of 'self' and 'other,' promoting internal peace and mental integration in contemporary life.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include dhyana (meditation) and consistent yoga-abhyasa to facilitate the merging of the individual consciousness into the universal consciousness.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Jivanmukti or dissolution of the ego (Ahankara) into the Brahman, termed as Samadhi through the process of Yoga.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the state of 'flow' and the reduction of cognitive dissonance by aligning the fragmented sense of self with a larger purpose or universal awareness.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: इत्थं च आत्माकारमनोवृत्ते स्थिरीभावः समाधिरभिधीयते इत्यर्थः । उक्ताभ्यां द्वाभ्यां श्लोकाभ्यां संप्रज्ञातः समाधिरुक्तः । सम्यक् सम्भूय विपर्ययरहितत्वेन प्रज्ञायते प्रकर्षेण अपरोक्षतया अनुभूयते भाव्यस्य स्वरूपमनेन इति संप्रज्ञातः समाधिः भावनाविशेषः । भावना च भाव्यस्य विषयान्तरपरिहारेण चेतसि पुनः पुनः निवेशनम् । संप्रज्ञातः सालम्बः सबीजः लयः - एते संप्रज्ञातस्य प्रसिद्धाः पर्यायाः ॥ ६ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: Thus, the stabilization of the mental modification in the form of the Self (Atmakara-manovritti) is termed Samadhi. Through these two verses, Samprajnata Samadhi has been described. It is called Samprajnata because by this, the nature of the object of meditation is known (prajayate) thoroughly and perfectly, without error, and experienced directly (aparoksataya). It is a special form of meditation (bhavana). Bhavana is the repeated placement of the object of meditation in the mind, while excluding all other objects. Samprajnata, Salamba (with support), Sabija (with seed), and Laya are famous synonyms for this state.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: इस प्रकार, आत्माकार मनोवृत्ति में स्थिरीकरण को ही समाधि कहा जाता है। उक्त दोनों श्लोकों द्वारा संप्रज्ञात समाधि का वर्णन किया गया है। इसे 'संप्रज्ञात' इसलिए कहा जाता है क्योंकि इसके माध्यम से ध्येय वस्तु के स्वरूप का सम्यक, विपर्यय रहित, प्रकर्ष रूप से अपरोक्ष अनुभव होता है। यह भावना (चिंतन) का एक विशेष रूप है। भावना का अर्थ है अन्य विषयों को हटाकर चित्त में ध्येय का बार-बार निवेशन करना। संप्रज्ञात, सालम्ब, सबीज और लय - ये संप्रज्ञात समाधि के ही प्रसिद्ध पर्यायवाची हैं।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi and Manolaya
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the cessation of the vital fluctuations (Prana) and the dissolution of the mind (Manolaya) as the precursor to spiritual absorption. This state signifies the withdrawal from external sensory engagement towards interior silence.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the psychosomatic connection where the stabilization of breath leads to mental clarity, a principle fundamental to contemporary mindfulness and meditation practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice described is Bhavana (repeated focus) and the cultivation of Laya (dissolution of breath and mind) to reach Sabija Samadhi.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept explains the Atmakara-manovritti where the mind, stripped of distractions (visyantara-parihara), rests in its source, manifesting as Samprajnata Samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychology recognizes this as the 'flow state' or autonomic nervous system regulation where controlled breathing (Pranayama) acts as a bridge to cognitive stillness and stress reduction.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Advaita (Non-dualism)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse encapsulates the core of Vedantic realization where the perceived division between the finite ego (Jiva) and the infinite consciousness (Paramatma) dissolves. It asserts that the ultimate state of being is one of homogeneous oneness (aikya) rather than separation.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This remains the cornerstone of Indian spiritual psychology, emphasizing that the goal of human life is to transcend the perceived limitations of the ego to align with the universal Self.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Nididhyasana (profound meditation), Atma-vichara (self-inquiry), and the cultivation of Samatvam (equanimity).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is Jiva-Paramatma-Aikya, which denotes the ontological non-duality of the individual consciousness with the absolute Brahman, attained through the dissolution of Upadhis.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological interpretation views this as the integration of the fragmented ego with the totality of consciousness, providing a pathway to resolving internal conflict, existential anxiety, and the sense of alienation common in postmodern life.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Ineffability of Higher Consciousness
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse highlights that the true state of Raja Yoga transcends intellectual grasp. It suggests that the depth of the meditative path can only be realized through direct subjective experience rather than theoretical knowledge.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In an era of information overload, this underscores the difference between reading about spiritual practices and the actual practice of silent inner inquiry.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Meditation (Dhyāna), Self-inquiry (Ātma-vicāra), and silent contemplation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Rājayoga-praśaṃsā' emphasizes the superiority and the transcendental nature of the royal path of yoga, which defies empirical categorization.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this validates the 'limitation of intellect' in understanding peak states of consciousness, shifting focus from conceptual learning to experiential phenomenology.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Vairagya (Dispassion) and Jnana (Knowledge)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse emphasizes that the path to liberation is difficult, requiring both the mental detachment from worldly objects and the intellectual/experiential grasping of the Ultimate Reality. It underlines that mere theoretical knowledge is insufficient without the foundation of radical detachment.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a reality check in spiritual life, encouraging aspirants to cultivate extreme patience and sincerity. In a modern context, it highlights the difficulty of maintaining focus and detachment in an era dominated by hyper-stimulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practices implied are Viveka (discrimination) between the permanent and impermanent, and Vairagya (dispassion) towards sensory pleasures, leading to meditative reflection (Nididhyasana) to achieve Tattvadarsana.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Vairagya (renunciation of sense-objects) as a prerequisite for Tattvajnana (realization of the Atman/Brahman). Without detaching the mind from external visayas, the intellect remains clouded, preventing the apprehension of the subtle Reality.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this verse addresses the 'attention economy' where constant sensory bombardment makes detachment (Vairagya) harder than ever. Cultivating mental distance from external stimuli is presented as the primary psychological strategy for clarity and mindfulness.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Sadhana and Yogic Discipline
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse emphasizes the multifaceted nature of the yogic path to achieve internal stillness. It highlights that the mastery of the mind requires a combination of physical postures, physiological control of breath, and specialized internal techniques.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: These practices remain the foundation of modern Hatha Yoga, helping practitioners stabilize the nervous system to achieve psychological equilibrium in a chaotic world.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice prescribes the rigorous training of the physical body (Asana) and the subtle life force (Pranayama/Kumbhaka) coupled with specific internal ritualized movements (Karana).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept focuses on 'Sadhana-upaya', identifying the auxiliary tools (Asana, Kumbhaka, Karana) as instrumental to the attainment of 'Samadhi'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern relevance lies in the psychosomatic regulation; these methods function as biofeedback mechanisms to regulate autonomic nervous system responses, proving effective in managing stress, anxiety, and autonomic dysregulation.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Jivanmukti and Kriya-Shakti
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the state of a liberated soul who has achieved internal enlightenment (Shakti-bodha). By exhausting the impressions of past deeds (Karma-kshaya), the individual attains a state of total freedom from the cycle of cause and effect.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It highlights the ideal of the 'Jivanmukta' in Indian philosophy, advocating for a transformation of consciousness that transcends mundane activity even while living in the world.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Meditation on internal energy (Shakti), cultivation of witness consciousness (Sakshi-bhava), and detachment from the fruits of action.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Shakti-bodha (awakening of consciousness-energy) and the attainment of Niskarmata (the state of being void of residual karma, or non-doership).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern psychological context, this equates to achieving mental equanimity and freedom from conditioning, allowing for intentional action rather than reactive behavior driven by past psychological trauma or habits.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Laya Yoga (Dissolution of the Mind)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the physiological and psychological confluence where the redirection of life-force into the central channel leads to the cessation of mental fluctuations. By withdrawing the mind into the state of 'Shunya' (Emptiness), the seeker transcends duality.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This remains the core of advanced meditation techniques where practitioners seek to balance the nervous system and achieve mental clarity through the regulation of prana, serving as an ancient precursor to modern neuro-feedback and mindfulness practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama (breath regulation), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), and Laya-Dhyana (meditation on dissolution).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Citta-Vritti-Nirodha' mediated by 'Nadi-Shodhana' and 'Sunyata'. It emphasizes the transition from active thought to the 'Akasha' (void) state, preserving the technical term 'Sushumna' as the axis of consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the state of 'flow' and the reduction of cognitive load. In a secular context, it provides a blueprint for stress reduction through the regulation of the autonomic nervous system via intentional breathing.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Jivanmukti (Liberation while living) and Transcending Time
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse acknowledges a Yogi who, through the mastery of Samadhi, has transcended the linear progression of time and the conditioning of Karma. By conquering 'Kala' (Time/Death), the individual attains the state of immortality even while embodied.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This concept highlights the human capacity for psychological freedom from anxieties related to the future and regret regarding the past. It suggests that deep meditative stillness allows one to transcend the temporal pressures of the material world.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Samadhi-abhyasa (the consistent practice of deep meditation and absorption) as the primary tool to dissolve the residue of past karmas.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya emphasizes the transcendence of Prarabdha-karma through Samadhi-abhyasa, leading to a state where the influence of Kala (time) is neutralized.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological interpretation views this as 'mindfulness-based emotional regulation' where one detaches from the deterministic cycle of past habits, attaining mental presence that makes one 'timeless' amidst stress.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi and Prana-nirodha
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes a causal link between psychological stability (citta-samatva) and physiological energy flow (madhyama-marga). When the dualistic fluctuations of the mind cease and the prana is directed into the central nadi, the practitioner enters the state of samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the Hatha Yoga core principle that the internal state of consciousness is mirrored by the breath's movement. Today, it serves as a basis for understanding how breath-regulation techniques (pranayama) directly influence neurological and psychological stress management.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Citta-vritti-nirodha (cessation of mental fluctuations) and Pranayama focused on guiding Prana into the Sushumna Nadi.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept addresses 'Sama-cittata' (equilibrium of mind) and 'Madhya-marga' (Sushumna channel). It posits that 'Siddhi' (attainment/perfection) is contingent upon the alignment of Vayu and Citta, marking the transition from Hatha Yoga techniques to Raja Yoga/Samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychology interprets this as the 'flow state' or 'homeostasis' where the autonomic nervous system reaches a state of balance. The emphasis is on the psycho-somatic connection where mental clarity and respiratory control are reciprocal.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
हठाभ्यासं विना ज्ञानं मोक्षश्च न सिध्यतीत्याह -
‘नानाविधैः विचारैस्तु न साध्यं जायते मनः ।
नानामार्गैः सुदुष्प्रापं कैवल्यं परमं पदं सिद्धमार्गेण लभ्येत, नान्यथा शिवभाषितमिति च । सिद्धमार्गो योगमार्गः । एतेन योगं विना ज्ञानं मोक्षश्च न सिध्यतीति सिद्धम् । श्रुतिस्मृतीतिहासपुराणादिषु चेदं प्रसिद्धम् । तथाहि -
‘अथ तद्दर्शनाभ्युपायो योगः’ इति, तद्दर्शनमात्मदर्शनम् । ‘अध्यात्मायोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति’ (क.उ २.१२)इति ।
‘श्रद्धाभक्तिध्यानयोगादेव हि’ (कै.उ. २) इति ।
‘यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् । तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिराम् इन्द्रियधारणाम् । अप्रमत्तः तदा भवति । ’ (क.उ.१०-११)
‘यदात्मतत्त्वेन तु ब्रह्मतत्त्वं दीपोपमेनेह युक्तः प्रपश्येत् ।
‘ब्रह्मणे त्वा महस ओमित्यात्मानं युञ्जीत’ (म.ना.उ.२४.२) इति
‘त्रिरुन्नतं स्थाप्य समं शरीरं हृदीन्द्रियाणि मनसा सन्निरुध्य ।
ब्रह्मोडुपेन प्रतरेत विद्वान् स्रोतांसि सर्वाणि भयावहानि ’ ॥ इति । (श्वे.उ. २.८)
‘ओमित्येवं ध्यायत आत्मनम्’ (मु.उ.२.२.६) इत्याद्याः श्रुतयः ।
यतिधर्मप्रकरणे मनुः -
‘भूतभाव्यानवेक्षेत योगेन परमात्मनः ।
याज्ञवल्क्यस्मृतौ -
‘इज्याचारदमाहिंसादानस्वाध्यायकर्मणाम् ।
महर्षिमातङ्गः -
‘अग्निष्टोमादिकान् सर्वान् विहाय द्विजसत्तमः ।
‘ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां स्त्रीशूद्राणां च पावनम् ।
दक्षस्मृतौ व्यतिरेकमुखेनोक्तम् -
‘स्वसंवेद्यं हि तद्ब्रह्म कुमारीस्त्रीसुखं यथा ।
महाभारते योगमार्गप्रसङ्गे व्यासः -
‘अपि वर्णावकृष्टस्तु नारी वा धर्मकाङ्क्षिणी ।
यदि वा सर्वधर्मज्ञो यदि वाप्यकृती पुमान् ।
यदि वा पुरुषव्याघ्रो यदि वा क्लैब्यधारकः ।
तरत्येव महादुःखं जरामरणसागरम् ।
भगवद्गीतायाम् -
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।
‘यत् साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानम्’ (५.५) इत्यादि च ।
आदित्यपुराणे -
‘योगात् सञ्जायते ज्ञानं योगो मय्येकचित्तता । ’
स्कन्दपुराणे -
‘आत्मज्ञानेन मुक्तिः स्यात् तच्च योगादृते न हि ।
कूर्मपुराणे शिववाक्यम् -
‘अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगं परमदुर्लभम् ।
योगाग्निर्दहति क्षिप्रमशेषं पापरञ्जनम् ।
गरुडपुराणे -
‘तथा यतेत मतिमान् यथा स्यान्निर्वृतिः परा ।
भवतापेन तप्तानां योगो हि परमौषधम् ।
स च योगाग्निना दग्धसमस्तक्लेशसंचयः ।
संप्राप्तयोगसिद्धिस्तु पूर्णोयस्त्वात्मदर्शनात् ।
आत्मारामः सदा पूर्णः सुखमात्यन्तिकं गतः ।
तपसा भावितात्मानो योगिनः संयतेन्द्रियाः ।
विष्णुधर्मेषु -
‘यच्छ्रेयः सर्वभूतानां स्त्रीणामप्युपकारकम् ।
इत्युक्तः कपिलः पूर्वं देवैर्देवर्षिभिः तथा ।
वासिष्ठे -
‘दुःसहा राम संसारविषवेगविषूचिका ।
ननु तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यैः अप्यपरोक्षप्रमा संभवतीति किमर्थमतिश्रमसाध्ये योगे प्रयासः कार्यः । न च वाक्यजन्यज्ञानस्य अपरोक्षत्वे प्रमाणासंभव इति वाच्यम् । तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यजन्यं ज्ञानमपरोक्षम्, अपरोक्षविषयकत्वात्, चाक्षुषघटादिप्रत्यक्षवदित्यनुमानस्य प्रमाणत्वात् । न च विषयगत-अपरोक्षत्वस्य दुर्निरूपत्वात् हेत्वसिद्धिरिति वाच्यम् । अज्ञानविषय- चित्त्वतत्तादात्म्यापन्नत्व-अन्यतररूपस्य तस्य सुनिरूपत्वात् । यथा हि घटादौ चक्षुःसन्निकर्षेण अन्तःकरणवृत्तिदशायां तदधिष्ठानचैतन्याज्ञाननिवृत्तौ तच्चैतन्यस्य अज्ञानविषयत्वं तद्घटस्य अज्ञानविषयचैतन्यतादात्म्यापन्नत्वं चापरोक्षत्वम् । तथा तत्त्वमस्यदिवाक्येन शुद्धचैतन्यान्तःकरणवृत्युत्थापने सति तदज्ञानस्य निर्वृत्तत्वेनैव चैतन्यस्य स अज्ञानविषयत्वात् चैतन्यस्य अपरोक्षत्वमिति न हेत्वसिद्धिः । न च अप्रयोजकत्वम्, ज्ञानगतापरोक्षत्वं प्रत्यपरोक्षविषयकत्वेन प्रयोजकत्वात् । न तु इन्द्रियजन्यत्वं, मनसः इन्द्रियत्वाभावेन सुखादिप्रत्यक्षे व्यभिचारात् । अथाभिव्यक्तचैतन्याभिन्नतया भासमानत्वं विषयस्य अपरोक्षत्वम् । अभिव्यक्तत्वं च निवृत्तवरणकत्वं परोक्षवृत्तिस्थले चावरणनिवृत्त्यभावात् नातिव्याप्तिः । सर्पादिभ्रमजनकदोषवतः तु नायं सर्पः किन्तु रज्जुरिति वाक्येन जायमाना वृतिस्तु नावरणं निवर्तयतीति तत्र परोक्ष एव विषयः । वेदान्तवाक्यजन्यं च ज्ञानमावरणनिवर्तकत्वात् अपरोक्षमेव । मननादेः पूर्वमुत्पन्नं ज्ञानमज्ञाननिवर्तकम् । प्रमाणासंभावनादिदोषसामन्याभावविशिष्टस्यैव तस्य अज्ञाननिवर्तकत्वात् । किञ्च ‘तं त्वौपनिषदं पुरुषं पृच्छामि’ (बृ.उ.३.९.२६) इति श्रुतिप्रतिपन्नम् उपनिषन्मात्रगम्यत्वं योगगम्यत्वे नोपपन्नं स्यात् । तस्मात् तत्त्वमस्यदिवाक्यादेव अपरोक्षमिति चेन्न । अनुमानस्याप्रयोजकत्वात् । न च प्रत्यक्षं प्रति निरुक्तापरोक्षविषयकत्वेन प्रयोजकात् तन्मूलकतर्केण अप्रयोजकशङ्कानिवृत्तिरिति वाच्यम् । लाघवात् जन्यप्रत्यक्षसामान्यं प्रति इन्द्रियत्वेन कारणतया तज्जन्यस्यैव प्रयोजकत्वात् । नित्यानित्यसाधारणप्रत्यक्षत्वे तु न किञ्चित् प्रयोजकमिति । त्वन्मते तु प्रत्यक्षविशेषे इन्द्रियं कारणं तद्विशेषे च शब्दविशेष इति कार्यकारणभावद्वयं स्यात् । न च मनसो अनिन्द्रियत्वं मनस इन्द्रियत्वे बाधकाभावात् ‘इन्द्रियाणां मनो नाथः’ (४.२९) इति तु, मनुष्यमेवोद्दिश्य मनुष्याणामयं राजा इत्यादिवत् इन्द्रियेष्वेव किञ्चिदुत्कर्षं ब्रवीति । न तु तस्य अनिन्द्रियत्वं तत्त्वं च षट्सु अखण्डोपाधिविशेष एव । अत एव ‘कर्मेन्द्रियं तु पाय्वादि मनोनेत्रादि धीन्द्रियम्’ इति (अ.को.१.५.८) । ‘प्रत्यक्षं स्यादैन्द्रियकम् अप्रत्यक्षमतीन्द्रियम्’ इति (अ.को.३.१.७९) च शक्तिप्रमाणभूतकोशोऽपि इन्द्रियाप्रमाणकज्ञानस्याप्रत्यक्षत्वं वदन् मनस इन्द्रियत्वज्ञापकः सङ्गच्छते ।
‘इन्द्रयाणि दशैकं च’ इति गीतावचनमपि (१३.५) मनस इन्द्रियत्वे प्रमाणम् । किञ्च तत्वमस्यादिवाक्यजन्यं ज्ञानं शाब्दं, शब्दजयत्वात्, यजेतेत्यादिवाक्यजन्यज्ञानवदित्यनेन अपरोक्षत्वविरोधिशाब्दत्वसाधकेन सत्प्रतिपक्षः । न चेदमप्रयोजकम् । शाब्दं प्रत्येव शब्दस्य जनकत्वेन लाघवमूलकानुकूलतर्कात् । त्वन्मते तु शब्दादपि प्रत्यक्षस्वीकारेण कार्यकरणभावद्वयकल्पने गौरवम् । अपि च मनननिदिध्यासनाभ्यां पूर्वमप्युत्पन्नं ज्ञानं तव मते अपरोक्षमपि नाज्ञाननिवर्तकमित्यज्ञाननिवृत्तिं प्रत्यप्रतिबद्धज्ञानत्वेनैव हेतुत्वमिति गौरवम् । मम तु समध्यभ्यासपरिपाकेन असंभावनादिसकलमलरहितेन अन्तः करणेन आत्मनि दृष्टे सति दर्शनमात्रादेव अज्ञाननिवृत्ते न कश्चितद् गौरवावकाशः ।
‘एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोत्मा न प्रकाशते ।
‘यच् छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञः’ (कठ.उ. ३.१२-१३) इत्यारभ्य अज्ञाननिवृत्यर्थकेन ‘मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते’ (३.१६) इत्यन्तेन कठवल्लीस्थमृत्यूपदेशेन संमतोऽयमर्थ इति न कश्चिदत्र विवादः इति । यदि तु मननादेः पूर्वमुत्पन्नं ज्ञानं परोक्षमेवेति नाप्रतिबद्धत्वकृतगौरवमिति मतमाद्रियते तदापि श्रवणादिभिः मनःसंस्कारे सिद्धे अव्यवहितोत्तरमात्मदर्शनसंभवात् तदुत्तरं वाक्यस्मरणादिकल्पनं महद्गौरवापादकमेव । ननु न वयं केवलेन तर्केण शब्दजन्यज्ञानस्यापरोक्षत्वं वदामः किन्तु श्रुत्यापि । तथा हि - ‘तं त्वौपनिषदं पुरुषं पृच्छामि’ (बृ.उ.३.९.२६) इति श्रुत्या चौपनिषदत्वं पुरुषस्य न उपनिषज्जन्यबुद्धिविषयमात्रं प्रत्यक्षादिगम्येऽाप्यौपनिषदत्वव्यवहारापत्तेः । यथा हि द्वादशकपालेष्वष्टानां कपालानां सत्त्वात् द्वादशकापालसंस्कृतेन अष्टाकपालादिव्यवहारः, यथा द्विपुत्रादौ एकपुत्रादिव्यवहारः, तथात्रापि । नान्यत्र तथा व्यवहार इति उपनिषन्मात्रगम्यत्वमेव प्रत्ययार्थः । तच्च मनोगम्यत्वे अनुपपन्नमिति चेन्न । न हि प्रत्ययेन उपनिषद्भिन्नं सर्वं कारणत्वाद् व्यावर्त्यते । शाब्दापरोक्षवादिना त्वयाप्यात्मापरोक्षे मनआदीनां करणत्वस्य अङ्गीकारात् । किन्तु पुराणादिशब्दान्तरमेव, ‘श्रोतव्यः श्रुतिवाक्येभ्यः’ इति स्मरणात् स चार्थो ममापि संमत इति न किञ्चिदेतत् । प्रमाणान्तरव्यवृत्तौ तात्पर्यकल्पनं चात्मापरोक्षे शब्दस्य प्रमाणत्वे सिद्ध एव वक्तुमुचितम् । शब्दान्तरव्यावृत्तितात्पर्यं तु श्रुत्यादिसंमतत्वात् कल्पयितुमुचितमेव । एवं स्थिते ‘मनसैवानु द्रष्टव्यं’ (बृ.उ.४.४.१९), ‘मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं’ (कठ.उ. ४.११) इत्यादिश्रुतयोऽप्याञ्जस्येन प्रतिपादिता भवेयुः । यत्तु कैश्चिदुक्तं दर्शनवृत्तिं प्रति मनोमात्रस्य उपादानपरायत्ताः श्रुतयो न विरुध्यन्त इति तदतीवविचारसहम् । यतः प्रमाणाकाङ्क्षायां प्रवृत्ताः ताः कथमुपादानपरा भवेयुः । ‘कामः सङ्कल्पो विचिकित्सा ....’ (बृ.उ. १.५.३) इत्यादिश्रुत्या सावधारणतया सर्वसां वृत्तीनां मनोमात्रोपादकत्वे बोधिते आकाङ्क्षाभावेन उपादानतात्पर्यकत्वेन वर्णयितुं कथं शक्येरन् । पूर्वं द्वितीयवल्यां प्रणवस्य ब्रह्मबोधकत्वेन उक्तस्यापि अपरोक्षहेतुत्वमिति शङ्कां निवारयितुं मनसैवानुद्रष्टव्यमित्यादि सावधारणावाक्यानीत्येवं वर्णयितुं शक्यानि स्युः इत्यलमतिवाग्जालेन । वस्तुतस्तु योगिनां समाधौ दूरविप्रकृष्टपदार्थज्ञानं सर्वशास्त्रप्रसिद्धं , न परोक्षम् । तदानीं परोक्षसामग्र्यभावात् । नापि स्मरणं तेषां पूर्वं विशिष्याननुभवात् । नापि सुखादिज्ञानवत् साक्षिरूपम्, अपसिद्धान्तात् । नाप्यप्रमाणकं प्रमासामान्ये करणनियमात् । नापि चक्षुरादिजन्यं तेषामसन्निकर्षात् । तस्मान्मानसिकी प्रमैव सा वाच्येति मनस इन्द्रियत्वं प्रमाणत्वं च दुरपह्नवमेवेति । येऽपि योगश्रुतयोः समुच्चयं कल्पयन्ति तेषामपि पूर्वोक्तदूषणगणः तदवस्थ एव । तस्माद् योगजन्यसंस्कारसचिवमनोमात्रगम्यः आत्मेति सिद्धम् । न च कामिनीं भावयतो व्यवहितकामिनीसाक्षात्कारस्येव भावनाजन्यत्वेन आत्मसाक्षात्कारस्य अप्रमात्वप्रसङ्गः । अबाधितविषयत्वात् दोषजन्यत्वाभावच्च । कामिनीसाक्षात्कारस्य तु बाधितविषयत्वात् दोषजन्यत्वाच्चाप्रामाण्यम्, न भावनाजन्यत्वात् । न च भावनासमाधेः ज्ञानजनकत्वे प्रमाणान्तरत्वापातः । तस्या मनःसहकारित्वात् प्रमाणनिरूपणनिपुणैः नैयायिकादिभिरपि योगजप्रत्यक्षस्य अलौकिकप्रत्यक्षे अन्तर्भावः कृतः । योग-अलौकिकसन्निकर्षेण योगिनः व्यवहितविप्रकृष्टसूक्ष्मार्थमात्मानमपि यथार्थं पश्यन्ति । तथा च पातञ्जले सूत्रे - ऋतम्भरा तत्र प्रज्ञा । श्रुतानुमानप्रज्ञाभ्यामन्यविषया विशेषार्थत्वात्’ (१.४८-४९) । तत्र समाधौ या प्रज्ञा सा ऋतं सत्यमेव पुरुषयाथार्थ्यं बिभर्तीति ऋतम्भरेति प्रथमसूत्रार्थः । सा समाधिप्रज्ञा श्रुतानुमानप्रज्ञाभ्यां श्रुतं श्रवणं शाब्दबोधः, अनुमननम् अनुमानं यौक्तिकज्ञानं तद्रूपप्रज्ञाभ्यामन्यविषया अतिरिक्तविषया । कुतः? विशेषार्थत्वात् । विशेषो निर्विकल्पोऽर्थो विशेषः यस्याः सा तथा तस्याः भावः तथात्वं तस्माच्छब्दस्य पदार्थावच्छेदकपुरस्कारेणैव अनुमानस्य व्यापकतावच्छेदकपुरस्कारेणैव धीजनकत्वनियमेन तद्ग्रहणयोग्यविशेष्यमात्रपरत्वादित्यर्थः । अत्र बादरायणकृतं भाष्यं - ‘श्रुतमागमविज्ञानं तत्सामान्यविषयम् । न ह्यागमेन शक्यो विशेषो अभिधातुं, कस्मात् ? न हि विशेषेण कृतसङ्केतः शब्दः’ इत्यारभ्य समाधिप्रज्ञानिर्ग्राह्य एव स विशेषो भूतसूक्ष्मगतो वा पुरुषगतो वा’ इति (१.४९) ।
योगबीजे -
‘ज्ञाननिष्ठो विरोक्तोऽपि धर्मज्ञोऽपि जितेन्द्रियः ।
किञ्च, ‘तदेव सक्तः सहकर्मणैति लिङ्गं मनो यस्य निषक्तमस्य’ (बृ.उ ४.४.६) इति श्रुतेः ‘कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु’ इति स्मृतेश्च (भ.गी १३.२१) देहावसानसमये यत्र रागाद्युद्बुद्धो भवति तामेव योनिं जीवः प्राप्नोतीति योगहीनस्य जन्मान्तरं स्यादेव मरणसमये समुद्भूतवैक्लव्यस्य अयोगिना वारयितुमशक्यत्वात् ।
तदुक्तं योगबीजे -
‘देहावसानसमये चित्ते यद्यद्विभावयेत् ।
देहान्ते किं भवेज्जन्म तन्न जानन्ति मानवाः ।
पिपीलिका यदा लग्ना देहे ज्ञानाद् विमुच्यते ।
योगिनां तु योगबलेन अन्तकालेऽप्यात्मभावनया मोक्ष एवेति न स्याज्जन्मान्तरम् । तदुक्तं भगवता ‘प्रयाणकाले मनसाचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव’ (भ.गी८.१०) इत्यादिना । ‘शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यः’(छ.उ.८.६.६) इत्यादि श्रुतेश्च । न च तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यस्य अपरोक्षज्ञानजनकत्वे तद्विचारस्य वैयर्थ्यमिति शङ्क्यम् । ’ इति ।
वाक्यविचारजन्यज्ञानस्य योगद्वारा अपरोक्षज्ञानसाधनत्वात् । अत्र च योगबीजे गौरीश्वरसंवादो महानस्ति, ततः किञ्चिल्लिख्यते ।
देव्युवाच -
‘ज्ञानिनस्तु मृता ये वै तेषां भवति कीदृशी ।
ईश्वर उवाच -
‘देहान्ते ज्ञानिना पुण्यात् पापात् तत्फलमाप्यते ।
पश्चात् पुण्येन लभते सिद्धेन सह सङ्गतिम् ।
ततः सिद्धस्य कृपया योगी भवति नान्यथा ।
देव्युवाच -
‘ज्ञानदेव हि मोक्षं च वदन्ति ज्ञानिनः सदा ।
ईश्वर उवाच -
‘ज्ञानेनैव हि मोक्षो हि तेषां वाक्यं तु नान्यथा ।
विना युद्धेन वीर्येण कथं जयमवाप्नुयात् ।
ननु जनकादीनां योगमन्तरेणापि अप्रतिबद्धज्ञानमोक्षयोः श्रवणात् कथं योगादेवाप्रतिबद्धाज्ञानं मोक्षश्चेति चेत् उच्यते ? तेषां पूर्वजन्मानुष्ठितयोगजसंस्काराज्ञानप्राप्तिरिति पुराणादौ श्रूयते ।
तथाहि-
‘जैगीषव्यो यथा विप्रो यथा चैवासितादयः ।
संप्राप्ताः परमां सिद्धिं पूर्वाभ्यस्तस्वयोगतः ।
धर्मव्याधादयः सप्त शूद्राः पैलवकादयः ।
मैत्रेयी सुलभा शार्ङ्गी शाण्डिली च तपस्विनी ।
एते चान्ये च बहवो नीचयोनिगता अपि ।
किञ्च पूर्वजन्मानुष्ठितयोगाभ्यासपुण्यतारतम्येन केचिद् ब्रह्मत्वं केचिद् ब्रह्मपुत्रत्वं केचिद् देवर्षित्वं केचिद् ब्रह्मर्षित्वं केचिन्मुनित्वं केचिद्भक्तत्वं च प्राप्ताः सन्ति । तत्रोपदेशमन्तरेणैव आत्मसाक्षात्कारवन्तो बभूवुः । तथाहि । हिरण्यगर्भवसिष्ठनारदसनत्कुमारवामदेवशुकादयो जन्मसिद्धा इत्येव पुराणादिषु श्रूयन्ते । यत्तु ब्राह्मण एव मोक्षाधिकारीति श्रूयते पुराणादौ तदयोगिपरम् ।
तदुक्तं गरुडपुराणे -
‘योगाभ्यासो नृणां येषां नास्ति जन्मान्तरादृतः ।
स्त्रीत्वाच्छूद्रत्वमभ्येति ततो वैश्यत्वमाप्नुयात् ।
अनूचानः स्मृतो यज्वा कर्मन्यासी ततः परम् ।
शूद्रवैश्यादिक्रमात् योगी भूत्वा मुक्तिं लभेत इत्यर्थः । इत्थं च योगे सर्वाधिकारश्रवणात् योगोत्पन्नतत्त्वज्ञानेन सर्व एव मुच्यन्त इति सिद्धम् । योगिनस्तु भ्रष्टस्यापि न शूद्रादिक्रमः ।
‘शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ।
अथ वा योगिनामेव ॥ (भ.गी ६.४१-४२)’ इत्यादिभगवद्वचनादित्यलम् ॥ १५ ॥
commentaries.text:
हठाभ्यासं विना ज्ञानं मोक्षश्च न सिध्यतीत्याह -
‘नानाविधैः विचारैस्तु न साध्यं जायते मनः ।
नानामार्गैः सुदुष्प्रापं कैवल्यं परमं पदं सिद्धमार्गेण लभ्येत, नान्यथा शिवभाषितमिति च । सिद्धमार्गो योगमार्गः । एतेन योगं विना ज्ञानं मोक्षश्च न सिध्यतीति सिद्धम् । श्रुतिस्मृतीतिहासपुराणादिषु चेदं प्रसिद्धम् । तथाहि -
‘अथ तद्दर्शनाभ्युपायो योगः’ इति, तद्दर्शनमात्मदर्शनम् । ‘अध्यात्मायोगाधिगमेन देवं मत्वा धीरो हर्षशोकौ जहाति’ (क.उ २.१२)इति ।
‘श्रद्धाभक्तिध्यानयोगादेव हि’ (कै.उ. २) इति ।
‘यदा पञ्चावतिष्ठन्ते ज्ञानानि मनसा सह बुद्धिश्च न विचेष्टते तामाहुः परमां गतिम् । तां योगमिति मन्यन्ते स्थिराम् इन्द्रियधारणाम् । अप्रमत्तः तदा भवति । ’ (क.उ.१०-११)
‘यदात्मतत्त्वेन तु ब्रह्मतत्त्वं दीपोपमेनेह युक्तः प्रपश्येत् ।
‘ब्रह्मणे त्वा महस ओमित्यात्मानं युञ्जीत’ (म.ना.उ.२४.२) इति
‘त्रिरुन्नतं स्थाप्य समं शरीरं हृदीन्द्रियाणि मनसा सन्निरुध्य ।
ब्रह्मोडुपेन प्रतरेत विद्वान् स्रोतांसि सर्वाणि भयावहानि ’ ॥ इति । (श्वे.उ. २.८)
‘ओमित्येवं ध्यायत आत्मनम्’ (मु.उ.२.२.६) इत्याद्याः श्रुतयः ।
यतिधर्मप्रकरणे मनुः -
‘भूतभाव्यानवेक्षेत योगेन परमात्मनः ।
याज्ञवल्क्यस्मृतौ -
‘इज्याचारदमाहिंसादानस्वाध्यायकर्मणाम् ।
महर्षिमातङ्गः -
‘अग्निष्टोमादिकान् सर्वान् विहाय द्विजसत्तमः ।
‘ब्राह्मणक्षत्रियविशां स्त्रीशूद्राणां च पावनम् ।
दक्षस्मृतौ व्यतिरेकमुखेनोक्तम् -
‘स्वसंवेद्यं हि तद्ब्रह्म कुमारीस्त्रीसुखं यथा ।
महाभारते योगमार्गप्रसङ्गे व्यासः -
‘अपि वर्णावकृष्टस्तु नारी वा धर्मकाङ्क्षिणी ।
यदि वा सर्वधर्मज्ञो यदि वाप्यकृती पुमान् ।
यदि वा पुरुषव्याघ्रो यदि वा क्लैब्यधारकः ।
तरत्येव महादुःखं जरामरणसागरम् ।
भगवद्गीतायाम् -
युञ्जन्नेवं सदात्मानं योगी नियतमानसः ।
‘यत् साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानम्’ (५.५) इत्यादि च ।
आदित्यपुराणे -
‘योगात् सञ्जायते ज्ञानं योगो मय्येकचित्तता । ’
स्कन्दपुराणे -
‘आत्मज्ञानेन मुक्तिः स्यात् तच्च योगादृते न हि ।
कूर्मपुराणे शिववाक्यम् -
‘अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि योगं परमदुर्लभम् ।
योगाग्निर्दहति क्षिप्रमशेषं पापरञ्जनम् ।
गरुडपुराणे -
‘तथा यतेत मतिमान् यथा स्यान्निर्वृतिः परा ।
भवतापेन तप्तानां योगो हि परमौषधम् ।
स च योगाग्निना दग्धसमस्तक्लेशसंचयः ।
संप्राप्तयोगसिद्धिस्तु पूर्णोयस्त्वात्मदर्शनात् ।
आत्मारामः सदा पूर्णः सुखमात्यन्तिकं गतः ।
तपसा भावितात्मानो योगिनः संयतेन्द्रियाः ।
विष्णुधर्मेषु -
‘यच्छ्रेयः सर्वभूतानां स्त्रीणामप्युपकारकम् ।
इत्युक्तः कपिलः पूर्वं देवैर्देवर्षिभिः तथा ।
वासिष्ठे -
‘दुःसहा राम संसारविषवेगविषूचिका ।
ननु तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यैः अप्यपरोक्षप्रमा संभवतीति किमर्थमतिश्रमसाध्ये योगे प्रयासः कार्यः । न च वाक्यजन्यज्ञानस्य अपरोक्षत्वे प्रमाणासंभव इति वाच्यम् । तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यजन्यं ज्ञानमपरोक्षम्, अपरोक्षविषयकत्वात्, चाक्षुषघटादिप्रत्यक्षवदित्यनुमानस्य प्रमाणत्वात् । न च विषयगत-अपरोक्षत्वस्य दुर्निरूपत्वात् हेत्वसिद्धिरिति वाच्यम् । अज्ञानविषय- चित्त्वतत्तादात्म्यापन्नत्व-अन्यतररूपस्य तस्य सुनिरूपत्वात् । यथा हि घटादौ चक्षुःसन्निकर्षेण अन्तःकरणवृत्तिदशायां तदधिष्ठानचैतन्याज्ञाननिवृत्तौ तच्चैतन्यस्य अज्ञानविषयत्वं तद्घटस्य अज्ञानविषयचैतन्यतादात्म्यापन्नत्वं चापरोक्षत्वम् । तथा तत्त्वमस्यदिवाक्येन शुद्धचैतन्यान्तःकरणवृत्युत्थापने सति तदज्ञानस्य निर्वृत्तत्वेनैव चैतन्यस्य स अज्ञानविषयत्वात् चैतन्यस्य अपरोक्षत्वमिति न हेत्वसिद्धिः । न च अप्रयोजकत्वम्, ज्ञानगतापरोक्षत्वं प्रत्यपरोक्षविषयकत्वेन प्रयोजकत्वात् । न तु इन्द्रियजन्यत्वं, मनसः इन्द्रियत्वाभावेन सुखादिप्रत्यक्षे व्यभिचारात् । अथाभिव्यक्तचैतन्याभिन्नतया भासमानत्वं विषयस्य अपरोक्षत्वम् । अभिव्यक्तत्वं च निवृत्तवरणकत्वं परोक्षवृत्तिस्थले चावरणनिवृत्त्यभावात् नातिव्याप्तिः । सर्पादिभ्रमजनकदोषवतः तु नायं सर्पः किन्तु रज्जुरिति वाक्येन जायमाना वृतिस्तु नावरणं निवर्तयतीति तत्र परोक्ष एव विषयः । वेदान्तवाक्यजन्यं च ज्ञानमावरणनिवर्तकत्वात् अपरोक्षमेव । मननादेः पूर्वमुत्पन्नं ज्ञानमज्ञाननिवर्तकम् । प्रमाणासंभावनादिदोषसामन्याभावविशिष्टस्यैव तस्य अज्ञाननिवर्तकत्वात् । किञ्च ‘तं त्वौपनिषदं पुरुषं पृच्छामि’ (बृ.उ.३.९.२६) इति श्रुतिप्रतिपन्नम् उपनिषन्मात्रगम्यत्वं योगगम्यत्वे नोपपन्नं स्यात् । तस्मात् तत्त्वमस्यदिवाक्यादेव अपरोक्षमिति चेन्न । अनुमानस्याप्रयोजकत्वात् । न च प्रत्यक्षं प्रति निरुक्तापरोक्षविषयकत्वेन प्रयोजकात् तन्मूलकतर्केण अप्रयोजकशङ्कानिवृत्तिरिति वाच्यम् । लाघवात् जन्यप्रत्यक्षसामान्यं प्रति इन्द्रियत्वेन कारणतया तज्जन्यस्यैव प्रयोजकत्वात् । नित्यानित्यसाधारणप्रत्यक्षत्वे तु न किञ्चित् प्रयोजकमिति । त्वन्मते तु प्रत्यक्षविशेषे इन्द्रियं कारणं तद्विशेषे च शब्दविशेष इति कार्यकारणभावद्वयं स्यात् । न च मनसो अनिन्द्रियत्वं मनस इन्द्रियत्वे बाधकाभावात् ‘इन्द्रियाणां मनो नाथः’ (४.२९) इति तु, मनुष्यमेवोद्दिश्य मनुष्याणामयं राजा इत्यादिवत् इन्द्रियेष्वेव किञ्चिदुत्कर्षं ब्रवीति । न तु तस्य अनिन्द्रियत्वं तत्त्वं च षट्सु अखण्डोपाधिविशेष एव । अत एव ‘कर्मेन्द्रियं तु पाय्वादि मनोनेत्रादि धीन्द्रियम्’ इति (अ.को.१.५.८) । ‘प्रत्यक्षं स्यादैन्द्रियकम् अप्रत्यक्षमतीन्द्रियम्’ इति (अ.को.३.१.७९) च शक्तिप्रमाणभूतकोशोऽपि इन्द्रियाप्रमाणकज्ञानस्याप्रत्यक्षत्वं वदन् मनस इन्द्रियत्वज्ञापकः सङ्गच्छते ।
‘इन्द्रयाणि दशैकं च’ इति गीतावचनमपि (१३.५) मनस इन्द्रियत्वे प्रमाणम् । किञ्च तत्वमस्यादिवाक्यजन्यं ज्ञानं शाब्दं, शब्दजयत्वात्, यजेतेत्यादिवाक्यजन्यज्ञानवदित्यनेन अपरोक्षत्वविरोधिशाब्दत्वसाधकेन सत्प्रतिपक्षः । न चेदमप्रयोजकम् । शाब्दं प्रत्येव शब्दस्य जनकत्वेन लाघवमूलकानुकूलतर्कात् । त्वन्मते तु शब्दादपि प्रत्यक्षस्वीकारेण कार्यकरणभावद्वयकल्पने गौरवम् । अपि च मनननिदिध्यासनाभ्यां पूर्वमप्युत्पन्नं ज्ञानं तव मते अपरोक्षमपि नाज्ञाननिवर्तकमित्यज्ञाननिवृत्तिं प्रत्यप्रतिबद्धज्ञानत्वेनैव हेतुत्वमिति गौरवम् । मम तु समध्यभ्यासपरिपाकेन असंभावनादिसकलमलरहितेन अन्तः करणेन आत्मनि दृष्टे सति दर्शनमात्रादेव अज्ञाननिवृत्ते न कश्चितद् गौरवावकाशः ।
‘एष सर्वेषु भूतेषु गूढोत्मा न प्रकाशते ।
‘यच् छेद्वाङ्मनसी प्राज्ञः’ (कठ.उ. ३.१२-१३) इत्यारभ्य अज्ञाननिवृत्यर्थकेन ‘मृत्युमुखात् प्रमुच्यते’ (३.१६) इत्यन्तेन कठवल्लीस्थमृत्यूपदेशेन संमतोऽयमर्थ इति न कश्चिदत्र विवादः इति । यदि तु मननादेः पूर्वमुत्पन्नं ज्ञानं परोक्षमेवेति नाप्रतिबद्धत्वकृतगौरवमिति मतमाद्रियते तदापि श्रवणादिभिः मनःसंस्कारे सिद्धे अव्यवहितोत्तरमात्मदर्शनसंभवात् तदुत्तरं वाक्यस्मरणादिकल्पनं महद्गौरवापादकमेव । ननु न वयं केवलेन तर्केण शब्दजन्यज्ञानस्यापरोक्षत्वं वदामः किन्तु श्रुत्यापि । तथा हि - ‘तं त्वौपनिषदं पुरुषं पृच्छामि’ (बृ.उ.३.९.२६) इति श्रुत्या चौपनिषदत्वं पुरुषस्य न उपनिषज्जन्यबुद्धिविषयमात्रं प्रत्यक्षादिगम्येऽाप्यौपनिषदत्वव्यवहारापत्तेः । यथा हि द्वादशकपालेष्वष्टानां कपालानां सत्त्वात् द्वादशकापालसंस्कृतेन अष्टाकपालादिव्यवहारः, यथा द्विपुत्रादौ एकपुत्रादिव्यवहारः, तथात्रापि । नान्यत्र तथा व्यवहार इति उपनिषन्मात्रगम्यत्वमेव प्रत्ययार्थः । तच्च मनोगम्यत्वे अनुपपन्नमिति चेन्न । न हि प्रत्ययेन उपनिषद्भिन्नं सर्वं कारणत्वाद् व्यावर्त्यते । शाब्दापरोक्षवादिना त्वयाप्यात्मापरोक्षे मनआदीनां करणत्वस्य अङ्गीकारात् । किन्तु पुराणादिशब्दान्तरमेव, ‘श्रोतव्यः श्रुतिवाक्येभ्यः’ इति स्मरणात् स चार्थो ममापि संमत इति न किञ्चिदेतत् । प्रमाणान्तरव्यवृत्तौ तात्पर्यकल्पनं चात्मापरोक्षे शब्दस्य प्रमाणत्वे सिद्ध एव वक्तुमुचितम् । शब्दान्तरव्यावृत्तितात्पर्यं तु श्रुत्यादिसंमतत्वात् कल्पयितुमुचितमेव । एवं स्थिते ‘मनसैवानु द्रष्टव्यं’ (बृ.उ.४.४.१९), ‘मनसैवेदमाप्तव्यं’ (कठ.उ. ४.११) इत्यादिश्रुतयोऽप्याञ्जस्येन प्रतिपादिता भवेयुः । यत्तु कैश्चिदुक्तं दर्शनवृत्तिं प्रति मनोमात्रस्य उपादानपरायत्ताः श्रुतयो न विरुध्यन्त इति तदतीवविचारसहम् । यतः प्रमाणाकाङ्क्षायां प्रवृत्ताः ताः कथमुपादानपरा भवेयुः । ‘कामः सङ्कल्पो विचिकित्सा ....’ (बृ.उ. १.५.३) इत्यादिश्रुत्या सावधारणतया सर्वसां वृत्तीनां मनोमात्रोपादकत्वे बोधिते आकाङ्क्षाभावेन उपादानतात्पर्यकत्वेन वर्णयितुं कथं शक्येरन् । पूर्वं द्वितीयवल्यां प्रणवस्य ब्रह्मबोधकत्वेन उक्तस्यापि अपरोक्षहेतुत्वमिति शङ्कां निवारयितुं मनसैवानुद्रष्टव्यमित्यादि सावधारणावाक्यानीत्येवं वर्णयितुं शक्यानि स्युः इत्यलमतिवाग्जालेन । वस्तुतस्तु योगिनां समाधौ दूरविप्रकृष्टपदार्थज्ञानं सर्वशास्त्रप्रसिद्धं , न परोक्षम् । तदानीं परोक्षसामग्र्यभावात् । नापि स्मरणं तेषां पूर्वं विशिष्याननुभवात् । नापि सुखादिज्ञानवत् साक्षिरूपम्, अपसिद्धान्तात् । नाप्यप्रमाणकं प्रमासामान्ये करणनियमात् । नापि चक्षुरादिजन्यं तेषामसन्निकर्षात् । तस्मान्मानसिकी प्रमैव सा वाच्येति मनस इन्द्रियत्वं प्रमाणत्वं च दुरपह्नवमेवेति । येऽपि योगश्रुतयोः समुच्चयं कल्पयन्ति तेषामपि पूर्वोक्तदूषणगणः तदवस्थ एव । तस्माद् योगजन्यसंस्कारसचिवमनोमात्रगम्यः आत्मेति सिद्धम् । न च कामिनीं भावयतो व्यवहितकामिनीसाक्षात्कारस्येव भावनाजन्यत्वेन आत्मसाक्षात्कारस्य अप्रमात्वप्रसङ्गः । अबाधितविषयत्वात् दोषजन्यत्वाभावच्च । कामिनीसाक्षात्कारस्य तु बाधितविषयत्वात् दोषजन्यत्वाच्चाप्रामाण्यम्, न भावनाजन्यत्वात् । न च भावनासमाधेः ज्ञानजनकत्वे प्रमाणान्तरत्वापातः । तस्या मनःसहकारित्वात् प्रमाणनिरूपणनिपुणैः नैयायिकादिभिरपि योगजप्रत्यक्षस्य अलौकिकप्रत्यक्षे अन्तर्भावः कृतः । योग-अलौकिकसन्निकर्षेण योगिनः व्यवहितविप्रकृष्टसूक्ष्मार्थमात्मानमपि यथार्थं पश्यन्ति । तथा च पातञ्जले सूत्रे - ऋतम्भरा तत्र प्रज्ञा । श्रुतानुमानप्रज्ञाभ्यामन्यविषया विशेषार्थत्वात्’ (१.४८-४९) । तत्र समाधौ या प्रज्ञा सा ऋतं सत्यमेव पुरुषयाथार्थ्यं बिभर्तीति ऋतम्भरेति प्रथमसूत्रार्थः । सा समाधिप्रज्ञा श्रुतानुमानप्रज्ञाभ्यां श्रुतं श्रवणं शाब्दबोधः, अनुमननम् अनुमानं यौक्तिकज्ञानं तद्रूपप्रज्ञाभ्यामन्यविषया अतिरिक्तविषया । कुतः? विशेषार्थत्वात् । विशेषो निर्विकल्पोऽर्थो विशेषः यस्याः सा तथा तस्याः भावः तथात्वं तस्माच्छब्दस्य पदार्थावच्छेदकपुरस्कारेणैव अनुमानस्य व्यापकतावच्छेदकपुरस्कारेणैव धीजनकत्वनियमेन तद्ग्रहणयोग्यविशेष्यमात्रपरत्वादित्यर्थः । अत्र बादरायणकृतं भाष्यं - ‘श्रुतमागमविज्ञानं तत्सामान्यविषयम् । न ह्यागमेन शक्यो विशेषो अभिधातुं, कस्मात् ? न हि विशेषेण कृतसङ्केतः शब्दः’ इत्यारभ्य समाधिप्रज्ञानिर्ग्राह्य एव स विशेषो भूतसूक्ष्मगतो वा पुरुषगतो वा’ इति (१.४९) ।
योगबीजे -
‘ज्ञाननिष्ठो विरोक्तोऽपि धर्मज्ञोऽपि जितेन्द्रियः ।
किञ्च, ‘तदेव सक्तः सहकर्मणैति लिङ्गं मनो यस्य निषक्तमस्य’ (बृ.उ ४.४.६) इति श्रुतेः ‘कारणं गुणसङ्गोऽस्य सदसद्योनिजन्मसु’ इति स्मृतेश्च (भ.गी १३.२१) देहावसानसमये यत्र रागाद्युद्बुद्धो भवति तामेव योनिं जीवः प्राप्नोतीति योगहीनस्य जन्मान्तरं स्यादेव मरणसमये समुद्भूतवैक्लव्यस्य अयोगिना वारयितुमशक्यत्वात् ।
तदुक्तं योगबीजे -
‘देहावसानसमये चित्ते यद्यद्विभावयेत् ।
देहान्ते किं भवेज्जन्म तन्न जानन्ति मानवाः ।
पिपीलिका यदा लग्ना देहे ज्ञानाद् विमुच्यते ।
योगिनां तु योगबलेन अन्तकालेऽप्यात्मभावनया मोक्ष एवेति न स्याज्जन्मान्तरम् । तदुक्तं भगवता ‘प्रयाणकाले मनसाचलेन भक्त्या युक्तो योगबलेन चैव’ (भ.गी८.१०) इत्यादिना । ‘शतं चैका च हृदयस्य नाड्यः’(छ.उ.८.६.६) इत्यादि श्रुतेश्च । न च तत्त्वमस्यादिवाक्यस्य अपरोक्षज्ञानजनकत्वे तद्विचारस्य वैयर्थ्यमिति शङ्क्यम् । ’ इति ।
वाक्यविचारजन्यज्ञानस्य योगद्वारा अपरोक्षज्ञानसाधनत्वात् । अत्र च योगबीजे गौरीश्वरसंवादो महानस्ति, ततः किञ्चिल्लिख्यते ।
देव्युवाच -
‘ज्ञानिनस्तु मृता ये वै तेषां भवति कीदृशी ।
ईश्वर उवाच -
‘देहान्ते ज्ञानिना पुण्यात् पापात् तत्फलमाप्यते ।
पश्चात् पुण्येन लभते सिद्धेन सह सङ्गतिम् ।
ततः सिद्धस्य कृपया योगी भवति नान्यथा ।
देव्युवाच -
‘ज्ञानदेव हि मोक्षं च वदन्ति ज्ञानिनः सदा ।
ईश्वर उवाच -
‘ज्ञानेनैव हि मोक्षो हि तेषां वाक्यं तु नान्यथा ।
विना युद्धेन वीर्येण कथं जयमवाप्नुयात् ।
ननु जनकादीनां योगमन्तरेणापि अप्रतिबद्धज्ञानमोक्षयोः श्रवणात् कथं योगादेवाप्रतिबद्धाज्ञानं मोक्षश्चेति चेत् उच्यते ? तेषां पूर्वजन्मानुष्ठितयोगजसंस्काराज्ञानप्राप्तिरिति पुराणादौ श्रूयते ।
तथाहि-
‘जैगीषव्यो यथा विप्रो यथा चैवासितादयः ।
संप्राप्ताः परमां सिद्धिं पूर्वाभ्यस्तस्वयोगतः ।
धर्मव्याधादयः सप्त शूद्राः पैलवकादयः ।
मैत्रेयी सुलभा शार्ङ्गी शाण्डिली च तपस्विनी ।
एते चान्ये च बहवो नीचयोनिगता अपि ।
किञ्च पूर्वजन्मानुष्ठितयोगाभ्यासपुण्यतारतम्येन केचिद् ब्रह्मत्वं केचिद् ब्रह्मपुत्रत्वं केचिद् देवर्षित्वं केचिद् ब्रह्मर्षित्वं केचिन्मुनित्वं केचिद्भक्तत्वं च प्राप्ताः सन्ति । तत्रोपदेशमन्तरेणैव आत्मसाक्षात्कारवन्तो बभूवुः । तथाहि । हिरण्यगर्भवसिष्ठनारदसनत्कुमारवामदेवशुकादयो जन्मसिद्धा इत्येव पुराणादिषु श्रूयन्ते । यत्तु ब्राह्मण एव मोक्षाधिकारीति श्रूयते पुराणादौ तदयोगिपरम् ।
तदुक्तं गरुडपुराणे -
‘योगाभ्यासो नृणां येषां नास्ति जन्मान्तरादृतः ।
स्त्रीत्वाच्छूद्रत्वमभ्येति ततो वैश्यत्वमाप्नुयात् ।
अनूचानः स्मृतो यज्वा कर्मन्यासी ततः परम् ।
शूद्रवैश्यादिक्रमात् योगी भूत्वा मुक्तिं लभेत इत्यर्थः । इत्थं च योगे सर्वाधिकारश्रवणात् योगोत्पन्नतत्त्वज्ञानेन सर्व एव मुच्यन्त इति सिद्धम् । योगिनस्तु भ्रष्टस्यापि न शूद्रादिक्रमः ।
‘शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ।
अथ वा योगिनामेव ॥ (भ.गी ६.४१-४२)’ इत्यादिभगवद्वचनादित्यलम् ॥ १५ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary asserts that without the practice of Yoga, neither knowledge nor liberation is achieved. It argues against the sufficiency of mere intellectual study (śravana/manana) without the 'fire' of Yoga to consume the obstacles (kleśas). The Bhashya extensively cites Upanishads, the Gita, and Puranas to prove that Yoga is the common thread in all traditions for purification and direct realization (aparokṣa-anubhūti). It concludes that while scriptural knowledge (śabda-jñāna) is a start, direct manifestation requires a mind stabilized in Samadhi.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: भाष्य का प्रतिपादन है कि हठाभ्यास (योग) के बिना न तो ज्ञान सिद्ध होता है और न ही मोक्ष। भाष्यकार ने अनेक उपनिषदों, गीता और पुराणों के प्रमाणों से यह सिद्ध किया है कि योग ही चित्त की शुद्धि और साक्षात्कार का एकमात्र उपाय है। शास्त्र-श्रवण मात्र से अज्ञान की निवृत्ति नहीं होती, उसके लिए योग-अग्नि द्वारा चित्त के मल का दहन आवश्यक है। योग ही वह परम औषधि है जिससे जीव जरामरण के सागर से मुक्त होता है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Yoga and Atma-Jñāna (Self-Knowledge)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse posits that intellectual knowledge remains sterile without the stabilization of the mind through Yoga. True realization (aparokṣa-jñāna) requires a mind cleansed of vāsanās (latent impressions) through meditative practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern psychology, this corresponds to the necessity of 'mindfulness' or mental regulation before deep insight or cognitive restructuring can occur, highlighting that intellect alone is insufficient for radical behavioral or spiritual change.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Hathābhyāsa (diligent practice), Samādhi (meditative absorption), Indriya-nirodha (restraint of senses), and constant ātma-bhāvanā (contemplation of the Self).
commentary_faqs.answer: Yoga-sādhana as the essential tool for aparokṣa-jñāna; the mind is not an inert instrument but requires saṃskāra through Yoga to become a mirror for the Atman.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The text bridges the gap between academic theory and practical mental health, asserting that conceptual understanding does not replace the experiential state of mental clarity required for psychological freedom.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
प्राणमनसोः लयं विना मोक्षो न सिध्यतीत्युक्तम् । तत्र प्राणलयेन मनसोऽपि लयः सिध्यतीति तल्लयरीतिमाह -
‘अभ्यासेन परिस्पन्दे प्राणानां लयमागते ।
प्राणमनसोः लये सति भावनाविशेषरूपसमाधिसहकृतेनान्तः करणेन अबाधितात्मसाक्षात्कारो भवति, तदा जीवन्नेव मुक्तः पुरुषः भवति ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: It has been stated that without the dissolution of Prana and Manas (the mind), liberation is not achieved. There, since the dissolution of the mind is attained through the dissolution of Prana, he describes the method of that dissolution: 'When the movement of the Pranas is dissolved through practice, the dissolution of the Prana and mind occurs. When there is a dissolution of Prana and mind, assisted by a Samadhi characterized by a specific meditation (bhavana-vishesha), there arises an unobstructed direct realization of the Self (Atman), and thus a man becomes liberated while still living (Jivanmukta).'

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Laya Yoga and Prana-nirodha
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse outlines the fundamental practice of directing vital energy into the central psychic channel, Suṣumnā. This control leads to the dissolution of mental turbulence, serving as a prerequisite for meditative absorption (Samādhi).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the physiological-spiritual intersection in Indian tradition, where somatic breath regulation is seen as a direct tool to influence the psychology of the mind, a practice mirrored in modern mindfulness and biofeedback techniques.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Abhyasa (consistent practice) to induce Prana-laya and the cultivation of Bhavana-vishesha (special focused contemplation) within Samadhi.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Prana-Manas-Laya (dissolution of life-force and mind). The Bhashya asserts that individual consciousness is bound by the movement (parispanda) of Prana, and liberation is the state where this movement ceases in the Suṣumnā.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the transition from the 'default mode network' (restless mind) to a state of 'flow' or 'equanimity' achieved through somatic regulation, providing a blueprint for stress-reduction and mental stability.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description: प्राणलये कालजयो भवतीत्याह - सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविति । सूर्यश्च चन्द्रमाश्च सूर्याचन्द्रमसौ । ‘देवताद्वन्द्वे च’ (पा.सू.६.३.२६) इत्यानङ् । रात्रिश्च दिवा च रात्रिंदिवम् । ‘अचतुर...’ (पा.सू.५.४.७७) इत्यादिना निपातितः । रात्रिंदिवम् आत्मा स्वरूपं यस्य स रात्रिंदिवात्मकः तं रात्रिंदिवात्मकं कालं समयं धत्तो विधत्तः कुरुतः । सुषुम्ना सरस्वती कालस्य सूर्याचन्द्रमोभ्यां कृतस्य रात्रिंदिवात्मकस्य समयस्य भोक्त्री भक्षिका विनाशिका । एतद्गुह्यं रहस्यमुदाहृतं कथितम् । अयं भावः । सार्धं घटिकाद्वयं सूर्यो वहति सार्धं घटिकाद्वयं चन्द्रो वहति । यदा सूर्यो वहति तदा दिनमुच्यते । यदा चन्द्रो वहति तदा रात्रिरुच्यते । पञ्चघटिकामध्ये रात्रिंदिवात्मकः कालो भवति । लौकिकाहोरात्रमध्ये योगिनां द्वादशाहोरात्रात्मकः कालव्यवहारो भवति । तादृशकालमानेन जीवानामायुर्मानमस्ति । यदा सुषुम्नामार्गेण वायुः ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे लीनो भवति तदा रात्रिंदिवात्मकस्य कालस्य अभवादुक्तं भोक्त्री सुषुम्ना कालस्येति । यावद् ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे वायुः लीयते तावद् योगिन आयुर्वर्धते । दीर्घकालाभ्यस्तसमाधिः योगी पूर्वमेव मरणकालं ज्ञात्वा ब्रह्मरन्ध्रे वायुं नीत्वा कालं निवारयति स्वेच्छया देहत्यागं करोतीति ॥ १७ ॥

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The commentary explains that overcoming time (Kala-jaya) occurs upon the dissolution of Prana. The Sun and Moon, defined by the dual Dvandva compound, create the day-night cycle. The Sushumna (the central nadi) acts as the devourer/consumer of this time generated by the solar and lunar rhythms. When the breath flows through the Sushumna and dissolves into the Brahmarandhra, the cycle of time ceases to exist for the Yogi. Thus, the Yogi who masters the Samadhi can intuitively know their time of death and transcend the limitations of the physical lifespan.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Kala-Chakra (The Cycle of Time) and Pranic Physiology
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse illustrates the metaphysical link between cosmic bodies (Sun and Moon) and the internal perception of time. It posits that time is not a linear absolute but a construct created by the rhythmic flow of vital energies (Prana) within the human body.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the yogic understanding of bio-rhythms, where the body's 'internal clock' is governed by the breath. Modern stress management and mindfulness are finding new resonance in this ancient concept of consciously slowing down the perception of time through breath control.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The prescribed practice is Nadi-shodhana or specialized Pranayama leading to the movement of Vayu into the Brahmarandhra, culminating in Samadhi.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Kala-Jaya (conquest of time) through the practice of Prana-Laya in the Sushumna-nadi, where the duality of Surya (Pingala) and Chandra (Ida) is transcended.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern psychological context, this relates to the 'flow state' and the subjective dilation or contraction of time, suggesting that metabolic regulation through meditative breath-work can profoundly alter an individual's stress levels and perception of mortality.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Sūkṣma Śarīra (Subtle Body Physiology)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the complex network of the subtle body, positing that human existence is defined not just by physical anatomy, but by a vast energetic architecture. The body is likened to a cage, emphasizing that life is an enclosed experience that relies on these seventy-two thousand energetic junctions for vitality.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this concept aligns with holistic views on psychosomatic health, suggesting that mental and physical health are inseparable from the movement of energy through the system, often explored in yoga and mindfulness practices today.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prāṇāyāma (regulation of breath), Nāḍī-śodhana (purification of channels), and dhyāna (meditation) to balance the flow through the vital gateways.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of nāḍī-jāla (network of channels) within the sthūla-śarīra (gross body), which serves as the conduit for prāṇa (vital energy) and caitanya (consciousness).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Understood psychologically as the interconnectedness of sensory inputs and autonomic nervous systems; it provides a framework for understanding stress, energy management, and the mind-body connection.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Kundalini Yoga / Prana-Agni Samyoga
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes the foundational mechanism of Yoga, where Prana (vital breath) is united with Agni (internal digestive/spiritual heat) to activate the dormant potential within the body. This union is the catalyst for the upward movement of energy toward higher states of consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It reflects the psychosomatic philosophy of Indian tradition, where physiological processes are consciously utilized for spiritual transformation, highly relevant in modern integrative mind-body health practices.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, Agnisara, and internal focus (Dharana) to harmonize the breath with the metabolic fire.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Prana-Agni-Samyoga, the fusion of vital life-force and internal heat, essential for the arousal of the Kundalini energy.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Understood psychologically, this represents the integration of 'vitality' (Prana) and 'will-power/focus' (Agni) to achieve peak performance and mental clarity, transcending simple physical regulation.

sanskrit_shloka: वायुः इति । यस्मात् परिचितः अभ्यस्तः वायुः तस्मादग्निना जठराग्निना सह कुण्डलीं शक्तिं बोधयित्वा अनिरोधतोऽप्रतिबन्धात् सुषुम्नायां सरस्वत्यां प्रविशेत्, वायोः सुषुम्नाप्रवेशार्थमभ्यासः कर्तव्यः इत्यर्थः ।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Kundalini Yoga
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the intersection of Hatha Yoga and internal alchemy, where the controlled breath (Vayu) acts as a catalyst to stir the latent spiritual energy (Kundalini). By aligning the physical breath with the internal digestive fire, the practitioner clears the central channel to achieve higher consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This is central to the Indian tradition of Samadhi-Nirupana, emphasizing that meditative states are not merely mental but physiological transformations rooted in the mastery of subtle energy channels.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Pranayama (breath control) and Abhyasa (diligent, sustained meditation) to remove Avarana (obstacles) in the energy channels.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Prana-Sanchara (movement of breath) into the Sushumna-Nadi, utilizing the Jatharagni (Vaishvanara) as a stimulus for Kundalini-Prabodhanam.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In a modern psychological context, this mirrors the concept of mind-body integration, where somatic regulation (breath) is utilized to achieve emotional and cognitive equilibrium, reducing the 'noise' of the nervous system.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Chitta-vritti-nirodha
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse posits an inseparable relationship between the rhythmic flow of the breath (Prana) and the oscillations of the mind (Manas). It suggests that the physiological regulation of breath serves as a direct instrument for achieving mental stability.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This is a foundational principle in Hatha Yoga and Raja Yoga, emphasizing the somatic control of the internal environment as a prerequisite for meditative absorption (Samadhi).

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, Kumbhaka, and focused breath awareness.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Prana-manas-samyoga', where breath and mind function as dual aspects of the same vital energy; controlling the 'Vayu' leads to the cessation of 'Chitta-vritti'.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychosomatically, this aligns with modern techniques of diaphragmatic breathing to regulate the autonomic nervous system, lowering cortisol and calming the amygdala to mitigate anxiety.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Brahmananda)
commentaries.description:
तदुक्तं वासिष्ठे -
‘द्वे बीजे राम चित्तस्य प्राणस्पन्दनवासने ।
तत्रैव व्यतिरेकेणोक्तम् -
यावद् विलीनं न मनो न तावद् वासनाक्षयः ।
न यावत् तत्त्वविज्ञानं न तावच्चित्तसंक्षयः ।
यावन्न वासनानाशः तावत् तत्त्वागम; कुतः ।
मिथः कारणतां गत्त्वा दुःसाध्यानि स्थितान्यतः ॥
त्रय एते समं यावन्न स्वभ्यस्ता मुहुर्मुहुः ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: It is stated in the Vasistha: O Rama, there are two seeds of the mind: the vibration of the vital breath and latent impressions. Furthermore, in their distinct relationship, it is said: As long as the mind is not dissolved, there is no cessation of vasanas. As long as there is no knowledge of the Truth (Tattva-jnana), there is no cessation of the mind. As long as there is no destruction of vasana, how can the realization of Truth arise? They act as reciprocal causes and are thus difficult to overcome until all three are practiced repeatedly and simultaneously.

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (Hindi)
commentaries.description: वासिष्ठ रामायण में कहा गया है: हे राम, चित्त के दो बीज हैं—प्राण का स्पंदन और वासनाएँ। इसी के संबंध में स्पष्ट किया गया है कि जब तक मन का विलय नहीं होता, तब तक वासनाओं का क्षय नहीं होता। जब तक तत्त्वज्ञान नहीं होता, तब तक चित्त का नाश नहीं होता। जब तक वासनाओं का विनाश नहीं होता, तत्त्वज्ञान कैसे हो सकता है? ये तीनों परस्पर एक-दूसरे के कारण हैं, इसलिए जब तक इनका बार-बार अभ्यास नहीं किया जाता, तब तक इन्हें सिद्ध करना अत्यंत कठिन है।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Chitta-vritti nirodha and the interdependence of mind and prana.
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse explains the Yogic principle that the mind is not an independent entity but is anchored by two forces: internal conditioning (vasana) and biological movement (prana). To master the mind, one must address both the psychological root and the physiological substrate.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This provides a theoretical foundation for Pranayama (breath control) and mindfulness, suggesting that psychological stability (mental health) is inextricably linked to physiological rhythms.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Prescribed practices include Abhyasa (repeated practice), Pranayama (to still the samirana), and Vichara/Jnana (to dissolve the vasanas).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around the 'Paraspara-karana' (reciprocal causality) between Vasana, Prana-spandana, and Tattva-jnana. The bhashya highlights that the Chitta is sustained by these forces in a circular trap.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Modern psychological perspective mirrors this in the 'mind-body' connection, where physiological arousal (breath/nervous system) and cognitive biases (vasanas/conditioned patterns) form a loop that can be broken through meditative intervention.

commentary_faqs.answer: This verse articulates the fundamental principle of Yoga: the interdependence of the mental activity (manas) and the vital breath (prana). When the mind is stilled or withdrawn into the source of consciousness, the physiological turbulence of the breath naturally subsides, leading to a state of internal equilibrium (Samadhi).

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes that self-regulation is not merely a mental exercise but a psychophysical process. In contemporary life, this highlights the necessity of addressing the body-mind connection for stress reduction and deep meditative states.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, Dharana, and Dhyana aimed at the stillness of mental fluctuations (cittavritti).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Manah-Prana-Nirodha' where the involution of the chitta into the atman results in the cessation of vayu-spandana (movement of breath).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Understood in modern terms as biofeedback and nervous system regulation, where psychological calm (the parasympathetic state) directly dictates heart rate variability and breathing patterns.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Sahacarya (Inseparable Concomitance)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse illustrates the concept of non-dual proximity between two entities, specifically Life (Prana) and Consciousness (Chetana). Just as water cannot be separated from milk once mixed, the animating force and the conscious principle are inherently entwined in every living being.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This serves as a foundational philosophical trope in Indian aesthetics and metaphysics to explain the synthesis of disparate elements, helping individuals understand the integrated nature of body-mind-spirit.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practices prescribed revolve around 'Samyama' and 'Antarmukha' meditation, focusing on the subtle observation of how breath acts as the carrier for consciousness.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Avinabhavini' refers to the inevitable concomitance where the existence of one implies the other; Prana (vital force) and Chetana (sentience) form a singular functional unit.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this reflects the psychosomatic unity, illustrating that our cognitive state (consciousness) and physiological state (breath) are bio-feedback loops that cannot be treated in isolation.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Prana-Citta-Sambandha (The Relationship between Breath and Mind)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse elucidates the symbiotic relationship between the biological rhythm (Prana) and the mental state (Citta). In yogic philosophy, the breath and the mind are viewed as two sides of the same coin; calming or stilling the breath leads to the cessation of mental fluctuations (Vrittis), and vice-versa.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This provides the foundational justification for Pranayama in yoga. In a modern context, it validates the psychological impact of breathwork (mindfulness breathing) on reducing anxiety and promoting mental equanimity.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Sadangayoga (six-limbed yoga) and specifically Pranayama techniques meant to induce the stillness of the Vayu.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya specifies that Prana-nirodha (cessation of breath) is achieved through Sadangayoga, emphasizing the causal link between Vayu (air/breath) and Chitta-vritti.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept bridges somatic regulation and cognitive behavioral health, suggesting that physiological control (breath) is an effective intervention for cognitive stillness (mental health).

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Svabhava (Inherent nature)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse identifies the intrinsic, restless nature of sensory inputs and the mind as the primary cause of internal distraction. It posits that restlessness is not an external accident but an inherent quality that must be understood to be transcended.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In the context of Samadhi (the eighth limb of Yoga), recognizing that the mind's fickleness is its 'natural' state prevents frustration in practitioners, shifting the focus from 'stopping' the mind to 'transcending' its nature through practice.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Viveka (discernment between the seer and the seen), and Abhyasa (constant practice to stabilize the restless mind).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of Svabhava (inherent nature) of the Manas (mind) and Rasa (sensory experience) is central to Citta-vritti-nirodha; the mind is 'cañcala' (restless) by its very constitution (guna-sattva-rajas-tamas).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Reflects the psychological reality of 'attentional bias' and the difficulty of focus in a stimulation-heavy environment; it validates the human experience of cognitive distraction as a biological/psychological default rather than a personal moral failure.

sanskrit_shloka: मूर्च्छतो हरते व्याधीन् मृतो जीवयति स्वयम् ।

translation: When one faints [in the state of Prāṇāyāma], it removes all diseases; when it dies [the breath becomes still], it revives the body itself.

तदेवाह -
तदुक्तं गोरक्षशतके -
यद्भिन्नाञ्जनपुञ्जसन्निभमिदं वृत्तं भ्रुवोरन्तरे ।
तत्त्वं वायुमयं यकारसहितं यत्रेश्वरो देवता ।
प्राणं तत्र विलाप्य पञ्चघटिकं चित्तान्वितं धारयेत् ।

commentaries.author: Jyotsnā (English)
commentaries.description: The text states that this is what has been taught in the Gorakṣaśataka: 'That which resembles a mass of collyrium (black ink), round, situated between the eyebrows, that reality is composed of Vāyu (air/Prāṇa), associated with the letter 'Ya', where the presiding deity is Īśvara. One should dissolve the Prāṇa there and hold it (Dhāraṇā) for five Ghatikas, accompanied by the Chitta (mind).'

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Prāṇāyāma and the Science of Prāṇa
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the yogic phenomenon where the control of the breath leads to a state of 'death-like' suspension (Kumbhaka). In this state, the inner vital force (Prāṇa) is purified, curing physical ailments and ultimately rejuvenating the practitioner.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It emphasizes the physiological and psychological impact of yogic breathing, relevant today for stress management, autonomic nervous system regulation, and mental clarity.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Kumbhaka (retention of breath), Bhru-madhya-dharana (focusing at the third eye), and the mental unification of breath with the deity Īśvara.
commentary_faqs.answer: The Bhashya focuses on Bhru-madhya-dharana (meditation at the eyebrow center) involving Vayutattva and the synchronization of Chitta with Prana, leading to a state of meditative absorption (Samadhi).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the transition from external sensory focus to internal 'quieting' of the mind, mimicking the reset of the nervous system similar to deep restorative sleep or meditative flow states.

sanskrit_shloka: मनस्स्थैर्ये स्थिरो वायुः ततो बिन्दुः स्थिरो भवेत् ।

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Prana-Mana-Bindu Synchronization
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the triadic relationship between the mind, breath, and vital energy. It posits that the fluctuations of the mind are directly linked to the fluctuations of prana, and their mastery is necessary to stabilize the bindu, which is essential for higher states of consciousness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This principle forms the physiological and metaphysical basis of Hatha Yoga and Tantric practices. It remains relevant as a precursor to modern mindfulness and breathwork techniques aimed at reducing cognitive agitation.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama (breath regulation), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), and Dhyana (meditation).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept of 'Manas-Prana-Bindu' unity where mental stillness leads to pranic regulation, fundamentally inhibiting the dispersal of biological and spiritual essence.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern psychology, this corresponds to the 'mind-body connection,' where physiological intervention through regulated breathing (vagus nerve stimulation) can directly alter cognitive states and emotional turbulence.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Pranayama and Mental Mastery
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse establishes a hierarchical relationship in the human subtle body: senses are guided by the mind, and the mind itself is stabilized by the life-force (Prana/Maruta). By controlling the breath, one gains mastery over the fluctuating nature of the mind.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This principle is the cornerstone of Patanjali's Yoga Sutras, emphasizing that regulation of the breath is the most direct method to attain mental focus, a practice widely utilized in modern mindfulness and somatic therapy.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama (breath regulation), Pratyahara (withdrawal of senses), Dharana (concentration).
commentary_faqs.answer: Prana-Manas-Indriya hierarchy; the mastery of 'Citta' through 'Pranavayu' (vital air) which acts as the 'Natha' (regulator) of the cognitive faculty.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Underlines the neuro-physiological link between respiratory patterns and emotional regulation; modern psychological 'top-down' vs 'bottom-up' processing parallels this ancient insight that regulating physical rhythm (breath) settles mental agitation.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Svarupa-Pratishtha (Resting in one's own nature)
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse asserts that the ultimate state of liberation (Moksha) is defined by the experience of one's own truth rather than by external labels or theological consensus. It encourages a shift from conceptual debate to direct experiential reality.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: It reflects the pragmatic approach of Vedantic and Yogic traditions, where spiritual achievement is measured by internal transformation rather than agreement with specific sectarian definitions.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Nishtha (steadfastness in one's meditative state), Avikalpa-bhavana (non-conceptual contemplation), and detachment from external validation.
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept addresses 'Moksha-vyavahara' (the nomenclature of liberation), suggesting that Svarupa-anubhava (the experience of self) supersedes 'mata-bheda' (doctrinal differences).

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this promotes internal locus of control and validates personal well-being and authenticity over the anxiety of seeking validation from societal or ideological norms.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi and Prana-nirodha
commentary_faqs.answer: The verse describes a state of profound yogic absorption (Samadhi) where the physiological functions of breath (Prana) and the psychological engagement with the material world (Vishaya) are neutralized. It signifies the transition from mundane consciousness to a transcendental state of absolute stillness.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: This reflects the pinnacle of Hatha and Raja Yoga, where the practitioner transcends the basic survival mechanism of the breath to access deep interiority, a state highly regarded in the meditative traditions of India.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: Pranayama, Pratyahara, and Dhyana leading to the spontaneous suspension of the vital air (Kevala Kumbhaka).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept is 'Prana-nirodha' (cessation of breath) leading to 'Chitta-vritti-nirodha' (cessation of mental fluctuations), where 'Vishaya-graha' (sensory grasping) is eradicated through the state of Asamprajnata Samadhi.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the state of 'flow' or deep cognitive detachment, where sensory overload is eliminated, allowing for the stabilization of the nervous system and the transcendence of reactive behavioral patterns.

commentary_faqs.question: Theme: Samadhi and Manonasha (Dissolution of Mind)
commentary_faqs.answer: This verse describes the state of a Jivanmukta where the active, manifesting mind (sankalpa) and the resultant engagement in worldly activity (cheshtita) have ceased. It posits that true liberation is not the performance of action, but the absolute cessation of the mental impetus that drives action.

commentary_faqs.question: Cultural & Practical Significance
commentary_faqs.answer: In modern times, this reflects the psychological state of 'flow' or 'deep mindfulness' where the ego-driven intent is removed, leading to a profound state of cognitive and emotional quietude.

commentary_faqs.question: Yogic Practice: The practice prescribed is the abandonment of intent (Nisankalpa) and the neutralization of sensory and motor activity (Cheshta-nirodha).
commentary_faqs.answer: The concept revolves around Manonasha (destruction of the mind) as a prerequisite for Samadhi, where Sankalpa (mental volitions) serves as the seeds of Samsara.

commentary_faqs.question: Modern Relevance & Therapeutic Benefit
commentary_faqs.answer: Psychologically, this represents the elimination of anxiety and executive burnout by detaching from outcome-oriented thinking, fostering a state of mental homeostasis and existential rest.
